tasks.title: Binding rules and policy
tasks.summary: Pure session-binding helpers, the small-change policy file with its overlay, and the registration of both new event types (declared and on the timeline).
tasks.objective: Add the pure rules of a session binding in a new module factory/orchestrator/src/sessionBinding.ts (the two event builders, the hook-only type list, the `/bs use` parser, name matching against the projects the factory knows, the newest-binding fold and its bounded tail form, the bypass-answer match, the policy read through the overlay rule and the reminder text), add the small-change policy file factory/policies/session-binding.yml, and register the two new event types: declared in FREE_EVENT_TYPES, listed in FREE_TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPES and mapped by eventKind in factory/orchestrator/src/db/queries.ts. No caller changes in this task.
acceptance_criteria: Epic criteria 1 and 7 (the record shapes): bindingInput returns an EventInput with actor 'user', event_type 'session-bound', the given session_id, project, causal_parent and plan_version, and payload {project, source: 'hook'} plus prompt_id when one is given; bypassInput returns actor 'user', event_type 'pipeline-bypass-approved', the given project and payload {project, question, answer: BYPASS_YES, prompt_id}; newestBinding returns the last session-bound event carrying the given cli_session_id and ignores other ids and other event types.

Epic criteria 3 and 11 (names): parseUseCommand returns {name} for `/bs use <name>` (later words ignored), {name: null} for a bare `/bs use`, and null for `/bs used`, `/bs status` and any text that does not start with `/bs use`; matchProject compares through normalizeProjectName and returns the known list's own spelling, so LEGACY_FACTORY_PROJECT matches FACTORY_PROJECT_NAME (both imported, never typed); knownProjectNames returns the names factoryProjects gives for a temp roadmap declaring project-a and project-b with checkouts under the M4 roots, omits a declared project with no checkout, and returns a list rather than throwing on an unreadable roadmap.

Epic criteria 4, 6 and 7 (reminder text): reminderLines(project, read) with read.ok returns lines that each start with REMINDER_PREFIX, name the project, say questions are free and every change goes through `/bs plan` and `/bs run`, quote policy.maxFiles, policy.maxChangedLines, BYPASS_HEADER and BYPASS_YES, say the question must name the files the change touches and its estimated changed lines, say one yes covers one change and a second change asks again, say the yes is recorded, and say nothing is blocked. With read not ok they still start with the prefix and name the project, name read.file, say it is missing or invalid, and say no small-change bypass is available this turn so every change goes through `/bs plan` and `/bs run`. reminderLines('project-b', r) equals reminderLines('project-a', r) with every 'project-a' replaced, and the joined text is at most 700 characters for a 40-character project name, in both forms (the not-ok form with a 120-character file path). unknownProjectLines(known) starts every line with the prefix and lists every known name.

Epic criterion 6 (policy, its override and its failure): bindingPolicyReadPath({repoRoot, overlayRoot}) over two distinct temp roots returns <overlayRoot>/factory/policies/session-binding.yml when that file exists and <repoRoot>/factory/policies/session-binding.yml when it does not. loadBindingPolicy() reads the file bindingPolicyReadPath gives for REPO_ROOT and OVERLAY_ROOT, and the shipped factory/policies/session-binding.yml reads to {ok: true} with two positive integers; a temp file holding max_files: 3 and max_changed_lines: 25 yields {ok: true, policy: {maxFiles: 3, maxChangedLines: 25}} and a reminder containing 3 and 25; a missing file yields {ok: false, file, problem: 'missing'}; unparsable YAML, a non-integer and a non-positive value each yield {ok: false, file, problem: 'invalid'}; none throws.

Epic criterion 7 (the yes): bypassRow returns {question} for the answer row whose header is exactly BYPASS_HEADER, whose answer is exactly BYPASS_YES and whose question is non-empty after trimming; a different header, a different answer, a change of letter case, and the yes with an empty or whitespace-only question each return undefined.

Epic criterion 8 (registration): FREE_EVENT_TYPES in factory/orchestrator/test/helpers/eventTypeScan.ts lists session-bound and pipeline-bypass-approved with writtenBy 'src' and a reason longer than 40 characters; both builders write the type as a string literal at the `event_type:` position, so the scan in test/eventTypes.test.ts sees it. FREE_TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPES in factory/orchestrator/src/db/queries.ts lists both, and eventKind returns 'Prompt' for both. In sessionBinding.test.ts, a temp log holding a session-start, a session-bound and a pipeline-bypass-approved event, projected into a temp db with openDb and rebuild, gives a timeline() whose rows include both types with kind 'Prompt'.

Test first, in factory/orchestrator/test/sessionBinding.test.ts (new), written before the module: under the null (main at 1cdb9aaf, no sessionBinding.ts) the file fails at import; after the change every case passes.

Test first, for the registration: with the builders written and no list entries yet, `pnpm run test` fails in test/eventTypes.test.ts ('every literal event type in src is declared somewhere') naming both types, and the timeline case in sessionBinding.test.ts finds neither row. Declaring them in FREE_EVENT_TYPES alone still fails ('every free event type reaches the operator timeline, or says why it does not'). Adding the FREE_TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPES entries makes the suite pass.

Revert proof: delete the two FREE_EVENT_TYPES entries and test/eventTypes.test.ts fails; delete the two FREE_TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPES entries and both test/eventTypes.test.ts and the timeline case fail; make reminderLines ignore its policy argument and the 3 / 25 case fails; drop the normalizeProjectName call and the legacy-spelling case fails; make bindingPolicyReadPath ignore overlayRoot and the overlay case fails; drop the empty-question check in bypassRow and that case fails; drop the files-and-size sentence from reminderLines and the reminder-text case fails.
Epic criterion 7 (trust model): HOOK_ONLY_EVENT_TYPES equals [SESSION_BOUND_EVENT_TYPE, BYPASS_APPROVED_EVENT_TYPE], in that order, and is the list task-4's `bs event append` guard imports.

Epic criterion 4 (bounded read, the fold): BINDING_TAIL_BYTES is 1048576. bindingFromTail(records, cli) walks the records newest first, skips records whose cli_session_id is not cli, and stops at the first of: a session-bound record (returns {project}), a user_prompt with payload.source 'hook' and a string payload.bound_to (returns {project: record.project}), a user_prompt with payload.source 'hook' and no bound_to (returns undefined); it skips every other type and returns undefined when the list runs out. On a log built of session-bound project-a, stamped prompts, session-bound project-b and stamped prompts, bindingFromTail over every suffix holding at least one binding or stamped prompt returns the project newestBinding returns over the whole log. Revert proof: drop the bound_to branch and the suffixes that hold no session-bound record fail.
Gates: `pnpm run test` in full, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm run lint`, then `bash scripts/check.sh` in full.

functional_clauses: Exports, fixed for the tasks that import them: SESSION_BOUND_EVENT_TYPE = 'session-bound', BYPASS_APPROVED_EVENT_TYPE = 'pipeline-bypass-approved', HOOK_ONLY_EVENT_TYPES: readonly string[], BYPASS_HEADER = 'Small change', BYPASS_YES = 'Yes, skip the pipeline', REMINDER_PREFIX = 'bs use: ', BINDING_TAIL_BYTES = 1048576, SESSION_BINDING_POLICY_DEFAULT_PATH, SESSION_BINDING_POLICY_PATH, bindingPolicyReadPath(roots: {repoRoot: string; overlayRoot: string}, exists?: (file: string) => boolean): string, interface BindingPolicy {maxFiles: number; maxChangedLines: number}, type BindingPolicyRead = {ok: true; policy: BindingPolicy} | {ok: false; file: string; problem: 'missing' | 'invalid'}, loadBindingPolicy(file?: string): BindingPolicyRead, parseUseCommand(prompt: string): {name: string | null} | null, matchProject(name: string, known: readonly string[]): string | undefined, knownProjectNames(input: {repoRoot, cwd, env, isClone, roadmapPath}): string[], newestBinding(events: readonly StoredEvent[], cli: string): {project: string; eventId: string} | undefined, bindingFromTail(records: readonly EventRecord[], cli: string): {project: string} | undefined, bindingInput({target, project, causalParent, planVersion, promptId?}): EventInput, bypassInput({target, project, causalParent, planVersion, promptId, question}): EventInput, bypassRow(rows: readonly Record<string, unknown>[]): {question: string} | undefined, reminderLines(project: string, read: BindingPolicyRead): string[], unknownProjectLines(known: readonly string[]): string[], notRecordedLines(): string[].

The policy follows the overlay rule paths.ts already uses for shipped-and-edited files (roadmap, lessons.md, stack.yml): SESSION_BINDING_POLICY_DEFAULT_PATH is REPO_ROOT/factory/policies/session-binding.yml (shipped, read-only), SESSION_BINDING_POLICY_PATH is OVERLAY_ROOT/factory/policies/session-binding.yml (the operator's copy), and bindingPolicyReadPath returns resolveOverlayRead(<overlayRoot path>, <repoRoot path>, exists). loadBindingPolicy's default argument is bindingPolicyReadPath({repoRoot: REPO_ROOT, overlayRoot: OVERLAY_ROOT}). paths.ts is not edited; the three names are built in this module from its exports.

loadBindingPolicy never throws: a missing file is problem 'missing'; a file that does not parse, or whose max_files or max_changed_lines is absent, not an integer or not positive, is problem 'invalid'; file is the path it tried.

knownProjectNames calls factoryProjects with the roadmap path given and the roots rule M4 uses in promptCapture.ts (resolveProjectsDir(repoRoot, cwd, isClone) and the work root's workspaces directory), and returns an empty list rather than throwing.

The builders set no cli_session_id themselves; the caller's appendWithin options stamp it, as capturePrompt does today. bypassInput sets the record project and payload.project from its one project argument.
notRecordedLines says, after the prefix, that the binding could not be recorded from this directory and that any earlier binding is unchanged.

The policy file holds max_files: 1 and max_changed_lines: 10 (added plus removed lines) under a header comment naming the epic, saying these are the numbers the reminder quotes, and saying an operator changes them with a copy at <work root>/factory/policies/session-binding.yml (in a clone, this file is that copy); the values are the operator's to change at sign-off (open question 1).
The module imports only node built-ins, yaml, events.ts, paths.ts, projects.ts and projectName.ts: nothing from db/, cli.ts or usage.ts, so the hook's import graph stays off the database layer.
The reminder text is built from the project argument, fixed strings in this module, the policy numbers, and on a failed read the file path only.

queries.ts edit is limited to the two FREE_TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPES entries (with a comment saying both are the operator's own acts, written by the capture hook) and the two eventKind cases returning 'Prompt'. No other line of queries.ts changes, and no export changes; task-5 edits the file after this task.
The OFF_TIMELINE_EVENT_TYPES and UNEMITTED_EVENT_TYPES lists in eventTypeScan.ts are not touched: both types are written and shown, so neither needs an excuse.

tasks.title: Capture writes the binding
tasks.summary: capturePrompt records `/bs use`, files and stamps bound home-log prompts under the project, and records the bypass yes with its question.
tasks.objective: Teach capturePrompt in factory/orchestrator/src/promptCapture.ts to append a session-bound event when the operator types `/bs use <known project>`, to file a bound session's home-log prompts and answers under the bound project and stamp them with the binding's id, and to append a pipeline-bypass-approved event carrying the answered question when a bound session's AskUserQuestion answer picks the fixed yes, all through the existing capture path and with nothing else about capture changing.
acceptance_criteria: Epic criterion 1: in a temp factory-shaped checkout resolved by M2 (and once by M1 through a temp BS_HOME), with a temp roadmap declaring project-a and project-b whose checkouts sit under the M4 roots, capturePrompt on `/bs use project-a` leaves exactly one session-bound event in prompts-<cli>: actor 'user', project 'project-a', cli_session_id the payload's session id, causal_parent an event of that log. A second `/bs use project-a` adds none; `/bs use project-b` adds one, and newestBinding over the log returns project-b.

Epic criterion 2: after `/bs use project-a`, the `/bs use` prompt and the next typed prompt filed in the home log carry project 'project-a'; after `/bs use project-b` the next prompt carries 'project-b' although its parent carries 'project-a'; an answer-mode user_prompt filed in the home log carries the bound project; a prompt filed in an existing epic log of the same cli id keeps that log's project; an unbound session's records are what main writes.

Epic criterion 3: `/bs use nothing-here` and a bare `/bs use` add no session-bound event, leave an earlier binding standing, and still record the prompt; `/bs use project-a` in a directory that resolves only by rule M3 adds no session-bound event.

Epic criterion 7: in a bound session, an answer payload with a row whose header is BYPASS_HEADER, whose answer is BYPASS_YES and whose question is non-empty leaves one pipeline-bypass-approved event in the answer's log with causal_parent = the answer user_prompt's event_id, payload.prompt_id = the tool_use_id, payload.question = that row's question text, and record project and payload.project both equal to the answer user_prompt's project. Repeating the same tool_use_id, picking another label, the yes with an empty question, and the same answer in an unbound session each add none. A session bound to project-a whose cli id also has an epic log of project-b gets the bypass event in that epic log with project 'project-b', so the epic log holds one project.

Test first, in factory/orchestrator/test/promptCaptureBinding.test.ts (new), written before the change: under the null (main at 1cdb9aaf) the session-bound count after `/bs use project-a` is 0, the next prompt has no project and no pipeline-bypass-approved event exists, so the criterion-1, -2 and -7 cases fail; after the change they pass. The epic-log, unbound and M3 cases are guards that pass before and after; their test names say so.

Revert proof: remove the binding-first precedence for home-log prompts and the `/bs use project-b` case fails; remove the bypass append and the criterion-7 case fails; let an M3 store bind and the M3 case fails.
test/promptCapture.test.ts, test/promptCaptureWrapper.test.ts and test/promptHookEntry.test.ts pass with no edit.

Revert proof for the bypass record: pass an empty question to bypassInput and the payload.question case fails; set the bypass event's project from the binding instead of the answer user_prompt and the epic-log case fails.

Epic criterion 4 (the stamp the bounded read relies on): every user_prompt filed in the home log of a bound session, in prompt and answer mode, carries payload.bound_to = the event_id of the binding newestBinding returns for that log, and the `/bs use` prompt carries the id of the binding written for it; prompts filed in an epic log and an unbound session's prompts carry no bound_to. Under the null no prompt carries bound_to, so the case fails; revert proof: drop the stamp and it fails.
Gates: `pnpm run test` in full, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm run lint`, then `bash scripts/check.sh` in full.

functional_clauses: On a prompt-mode payload whose prompt parseUseCommand reads as a name that matchProject finds in knownProjectNames for this turn's context, in a store resolved by M1, M2 or M4: append bindingInput to the home log prompts-<cli> of that store before the prompt's own user_prompt is built, unless newestBinding of that log already names the project. A home log with no events gets its session-start root first, written the way the home-log prompt path writes it today; causal_parent is the newest main-thread event of the home log for this cli, else its root.
The binding is read with readEvents from the home log of the resolved store, and written there only; no other file, variable or table holds a binding.

Project precedence for a user_prompt filed in the home log of a bound session: the binding's project, then the parent's, then the declared project, then the root's. Filing in an epic log is unchanged.
In a bound session, a user_prompt filed in the home log gets payload.bound_to = the newest binding's event_id; nothing else about its payload changes. Epic-log prompts get no stamp.

In answer mode in a bound session, when bypassRow(answers) matches, the same appendWithin callback that returns the answer's user_prompt also returns bypassInput with causalParent = the id that user_prompt is stored under, question = bypassRow's question, and project = the project that user_prompt is filed with (the same variable), so the bypass event in an epic log takes that log's project; when the callback returns [] for a duplicate, it returns no bypass event either.
keeps_exports: every export promptCapture.ts has at 1cdb9aaf keeps its name and signature, because task-3 imports them concurrently; new exports are allowed.
The return line keeps its format, `bs prompt capture: ` followed by the event_id and session_id of the user_prompt written.
No change to resolveCaptureStore's rules, to dedupe, to the epic-log scan, or to the cli.ts verb `bs prompt capture`, which reaches this code unchanged.

tasks.title: Reminder on every turn
tasks.summary: The hook prints the binding reminder from a bounded tail read, independent of the capture, exit 0, plain text, never a hook decision.
tasks.objective: Print the binding reminder on every prompt turn of a bound session from the hook process: a new module factory/orchestrator/src/bindingReminder.ts computes the lines from the payload and a bounded tail of the session's home log, and runs the capture and the reminder as two independent steps; factory/orchestrator/src/promptHook.ts prints what they return, so the hook keeps exiting 0 with plain-text stdout whatever happens and a large log never costs the capture its line.
acceptance_criteria: Epic criterion 4: bindingReminder on a prompt-mode payload in a temp M2 store whose home log holds a session-bound event for the payload's cli id (seeded with bindingInput and appendWithin) returns reminderLines(project, loadBindingPolicy()); with no binding it returns []; with only another cli id's binding it returns [].

Epic criterion 3: for `/bs use nothing-here` it returns unknownProjectLines(known), followed by the standing binding's reminder when there is one, and no returned line contains 'nothing-here' or a unique marker word placed later in the prompt; for a matched name the newest binding does not name it returns notRecordedLines() followed by the standing binding's reminder, if any; for `/bs use project-a` in a directory with no store or an M3-only store it returns notRecordedLines().

Epic criterion 4, independence from the capture: the built hook prints the reminder lines for a bound session on a duplicate prompt (the capture writes nothing and prints no capture line) and on a harness-text prompt.

Epic criterion 5, in factory/orchestrator/test/promptHookEntry.test.ts against dist/promptHook.js: for a bound session (seeded binding), an unbound session, `/bs use nothing-here`, and an internal failure (the home log replaced by a line that is not JSON), the process exits 0, every stdout line starts with `bs prompt capture: ` or REMINDER_PREFIX, and JSON.parse throws on every stdout line, so no line carries decision, continue, hookSpecificOutput or permissionDecision. Answer mode in a bound session prints no reminder line. The file's existing cases keep their expectations, including 'does not reach the database layer'.

Operator decision 5, one capture path (supports epic criteria 4 and 5): bindingReminder writes nothing (the store directory listing is identical before and after a call), and promptHook reads stdin once and hands the same text to capturePrompt and bindingReminder; .claude/hooks/hooks.json and .claude/hooks/prompt-capture.sh are untouched.

Test first, in factory/orchestrator/test/bindingReminder.test.ts (new) and the new cases of test/promptHookEntry.test.ts, written before the change: under the null (main at 1cdb9aaf) the module import fails and the built hook prints no `bs use: ` line for a bound session, a duplicate prompt or an unknown name, so those cases fail; after the change they pass. The exit-status and no-JSON checks for the unbound and internal-failure cases are guards that pass before and after; their test names say so.

Revert proof: print the reminder only when capturePrompt returned a line and the duplicate-prompt case fails; let a reminder error escape its try/catch and the internal-failure case fails on exit status.

Epic criterion 4, bounded read (large-log fixture): a temp M2 home log holds a session-start, a session-bound project-a for the payload's cli id, then a line that is not JSON, then more than 4 MiB of user_prompt records for that cli id with project 'project-a', payload.source 'hook' and payload.bound_to set, written directly with appendFileSync, so the bad line ends more than BINDING_TAIL_BYTES before the end of the file. bindingReminder on a prompt in that store returns reminderLines('project-a', loadBindingPolicy()), and the built hook on that store prints those lines and exits 0, whatever the capture does with that log. A whole-log read throws on the bad line, so under the null (and for a version that calls readEvents on the home log) both cases fail. The stated bound: on a turn that is not a `/bs use` command the reminder reads at most BINDING_TAIL_BYTES of the home log plus the policy file, after the store resolution the capture already does. Revert proof: read the binding with readEvents over the whole home log and both cases fail.

Epic criterion 4, each step alone: promptTurnLines(raw, ctx, steps) with a capture step that throws still returns the reminder step's lines; with a reminder step that throws it still returns the capture step's line; with both throwing it returns []; with both succeeding it returns the capture line then the reminder lines. Under the null the module is absent, so the cases fail; revert proof: run both steps inside one try/catch and the throwing-capture case fails.
Gates: `pnpm run build` (the entry tests read dist), `pnpm run test` in full, `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run typecheck:test`, `pnpm run lint`, then `bash scripts/check.sh` in full.

functional_clauses: bindingReminder(raw: string, ctx: CaptureContext): Promise<string[]> parses the payload as capturePrompt does (a JSON object, session_id matching CLI_ID, no agent_id, a string prompt) and returns [] for anything else; resolves the store with resolveCaptureStore using the payload cwd when present and the prompt's command token; reads the binding from the home log file <eventsDir>/prompts-<cli>.jsonl (the file readEvents('prompts-<cli>', {stateDir: eventsDir}) reads) with one positioned read of at most BINDING_TAIL_BYTES from its end, drops the window's first line unless the window starts at offset 0, parses each complete line (a line that is not JSON throws, which promptTurnLines catches), and folds with bindingFromTail; it never calls readEvents on the home log. It may throw on a store failure.

Line selection, with the binding taken from bindingFromTail: a `/bs use` prompt with no store or an M3 store gives notRecordedLines(); a `/bs use` prompt with a null or unmatched name gives unknownProjectLines(knownProjectNames(...)) then the standing binding's reminder; a matched name the binding names gives its reminder; a matched name the binding does not name gives notRecordedLines() then the standing binding's reminder; any other prompt in a store resolved by M1, M2 or M4 with a binding gives reminderLines(binding.project, loadBindingPolicy()); everything else gives []. knownProjectNames (the roadmap) is read only on a `/bs use` turn.

promptTurnLines(raw: string, ctx: CaptureContext, steps = {capture: (r, c) => capturePrompt(r, c, 'prompt'), reminder: bindingReminder}): Promise<string[]> lives in bindingReminder.ts; it runs steps.capture then steps.reminder, each awaited inside its own try/catch, and returns the capture line when it is a non-null string followed by the reminder lines.

tasks.title: /bs use playbook and append guard
tasks.summary: SKILL.md routes `/bs use <project>` to a new use.md playbook, pinned by a test; `bs event append` refuses the two hook-only event types.
tasks.objective: Add `/bs use <project>` to the operator console: a row in the subcommand table and a word in the description of .claude/skills/bs/SKILL.md, and a new playbook .claude/skills/bs/use.md telling the session what to do with the hook's `bs use:` lines and how to ask for one small change, with a test that pins the routing and keeps the reminder the one copy of the bypass wording.
